purpose: Teach: 年来/腫れ/固まり/がんばろ/いただこ/叫び声/過ごさ/細やか

lines.speaker: mei_romantic
lines.jp: 翔くん、メイ姉さん、ママの五年来の友達よ。
lines.en: Sho, Mei is your mom's friend from way back — they've known each other five years now.
lines.style: Warm, matter-of-fact introduction. Gentle pace. Natural breath between clauses. Tender but not precious.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: うん。手、ちょっと腫れてるよ、メイ姉さん。
lines.en: Yeah. Your hand's a little swollen though, Mei-sis.
lines.style: Soft, observant. Not alarmed—just noticing what's true. Gentle concern embedded in simple words. Eyes down slightly, checking her hand.

lines.speaker: mei_romantic
lines.jp: 公園の池、氷の固まりが、浮いていたわね。
lines.en: There were chunks of ice floating on the pond in the park.
lines.style: Distant, thoughtful. Speaking more to herself than to him. Slow, measured. A small pause after 'pond'—remembering something.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 宿題、一緒にがんばろう、メイ姉さん!
lines.style: Bright, hopeful energy. Quick attack on the opening. Eager without being demanding. A small lift at the end—inviting, not insisting.

lines.speaker: mei_romantic
lines.jp: お土産のクッキー、いただこうかな。
lines.en: Maybe I'll have one of those souvenir cookies.
lines.style: Soft, pleased. A small smile in the voice. Unhurried. Comfortable silence possible after this line.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 昨日、公園で、子供の叫び声、聞こえたよ。
lines.en: Yesterday I heard a kid screaming in the park.
lines.style: Slightly animated, a little uncertain. Like he's still processing what he heard. Small hesitation before 'screaming'—not quite fear, just checking if it's okay to mention it.

lines.speaker: mei_romantic
lines.jp: 休日、ぼーっとして過ごさないようにしているの。
lines.en: I try not to let holidays turn into total blank time.
lines.style: Quiet, intentional. Speaking from something real. Not defensive, but sincere. A pause before 'blank time'—choosing the right words.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: メイ姉さんの編み物、細やかで、すごい!
lines.en: Your knitting is so delicate, Mei-sis. You're really good at it.
lines.style: Genuine admiration, slightly in awe. Slow, appreciative pace. Focus and warmth in equal measure. Not performing praise—just saying what he sees.
